passage_text: Researchers investigated the influence of different monochromatic light wavelengths on the growth of the freshwater alga *Chlorella vulgaris*. Cultures were grown in identical photobioreactors under controlled temperature (25 °C) and CO₂ concentration (2 %). Five wavelengths (400 nm, 450 nm, 500 nm, 550 nm, 600 nm) were applied for 14 days, with a dark control. Growth was measured as the daily increase in cell density (×10⁶ cells/mL per day), photosynthetic efficiency (PE) via chlorophyll fluorescence, and final biomass concentration (g/L). The results suggested a peak in growth and PE at 450 nm, while 550 nm produced the lowest values. The study aimed to identify optimal illumination for maximizing algal productivity in biofuel production.
table_data:
Wavelength (nm) | Growth Rate (×10⁶ cells/mL per day) | Photosynthetic Efficiency (%) | Biomass (g/L)
400 | 1.5 | 55 | 1.10
450 | 1.9 | 68 | 1.35
500 | 1.2 | 45 | 0.85
550 | 0.9 | 35 | 0.70
600 | 1.6 | 60 | 1.20
stem: Which wavelength produced the highest growth rate in the study?
explanation: The table shows a growth rate of 1.9 × 10⁶ cells/mL per day at 450 nm, higher than all other wavelengths.
trap: Choosing 600 nm because orange-red light is often described as most effective for photosynthesis, although its growth rate (1.6) was below that at 450 nm (1.9).

stem: Which of the following would be the most appropriate control for this experiment?

options.A: A culture illuminated with 500 nm light for 7 days
options.B: A culture kept in complete darkness for 14 days
options.C: A culture illuminated with 550 nm light for 14 days
options.D: A culture illuminated with 400 nm light for 14 days

explanation: A dark control establishes the baseline growth without light, allowing comparison of light-induced effects.
trap: Students may choose a light wavelength as control, but the study already tests multiple wavelengths; the only true baseline is darkness.

stem: What is the average growth rate across all five wavelengths?
explanation: Correct: B) (1.5 + 1.9 + 1.2 + 0.9 + 1.6)/5 = 7.1/5 = 1.42 × 10⁶ cells/mL per day. Why the others are wrong: A) 1.32 is not the mean of the five rates. C) 1.48 is not the mean of the five rates. D) 1.56 is close to the 600 nm value (1.6) rather than the mean of all five.
trap: Estimating near the middle value (about 1.5) instead of summing all five rates (7.1) and dividing by 5.

stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding the study?

options.A: The experiment controlled for temperature and CO₂ concentration.
options.B: The highest photosynthetic efficiency was observed at 600 nm.
options.C: A dark control was included to assess baseline growth.
options.D: Growth rates were expressed as increases in cell density per day.

explanation: Correct: B) The highest photosynthetic efficiency was 68% at 450 nm; 600 nm gave 60%, so the statement is false. Why the others are wrong: A) the passage states that temperature (25 °C) and CO₂ (2%) were controlled. C) the passage states that a dark control was included. D) the passage states that growth was measured as the daily increase in cell density.
trap: Assuming 600 nm had the highest efficiency because its growth (1.6) is the second highest; the table shows the highest PE (68%) at 450 nm.
